quickAnswer: Nationally, commercial breakroom and appliance deep cleaning runs about $0.35–$0.90 per sq ft of breakroom floor area, $25–$85 per major appliance (refrigerator, dishwasher, oven, ice machine exterior), or $35–$65 per labor hour for standard crews and $55–$95 for specialty degreasing. Most vendors apply a $90–$135 minimum per visit, so a typical 300 sq ft breakroom with four appliances costs $180–$420 per deep clean.

blocks.text: What a breakroom deep clean covers, and what nightly service does not

Most office contracts include a routine breakroom pass priced at about $12–$25 per visit: wiping counters, cleaning the sink, wiping the microwave inside and out, wiping the refrigerator exterior, and sanitizing cabinet pulls. A deep clean goes much further. Crews empty and clean refrigerator interiors and gaskets, pull dishwasher filters and wipe spray arms, degrease microwave ceilings and range hoods, descale coffee brewers and water dispensers where the equipment contract allows, scrub grout or VCT under appliances, wipe cabinet fronts and toe kicks, and sanitize trash enclosures. It is labor-heavy, detail work, which is why it is priced separately.

blocks.text: Per-appliance pricing varies with size and condition. A full-size refrigerator with an interior clean-out, gasket scrub, and coil vacuuming sits at the top of the range, around $60–$85. Countertop microwaves and under-counter dishwashers fall near $25–$45. Commercial ice machines should only receive exterior cleaning and bin sanitizing from janitors; interior descaling belongs to the equipment service contract.

blocks.title: Benchmark worked example
blocks.text: A 300 sq ft breakroom with a full-size fridge, dishwasher, two microwaves, and a coffee station takes a two-person crew about 2.5–3.5 hours, or 5–7 labor hours. At $35–$65 per hour, that is $175–$455. Per sq ft at $0.35–$0.90 yields $105–$270, which a vendor would raise to cover appliances, so expect actual quotes around $180–$420.
How minimum charges change the math for small kitchenettes

Minimum charges matter most for small suites. A 120 sq ft kitchenette with one fridge and one microwave may only need about 1.5 labor hours, which works out to $53–$98 at standard rates. Most vendors will apply their $90–$135 minimum, so the effective price is close to the minimum regardless of the unit math. The way around this is to bundle the deep clean with the nightly visit or with another periodic task such as interior glass or carpet spotting, so the minimum covers more work. Read the contract to confirm the minimum serves as a floor, not an extra charge on top of unit pricing.
Converting deep cleans into a monthly budget line

Once you pick a frequency, add the deep clean to your routine breakroom add-on to get a full monthly cost. On a five-night contract, the routine breakroom pass at $12–$25 per visit across 21.65 visits per month (5 × 4.33 weeks) costs $260–$541 per month. Add a monthly deep clean at $180–$420 and the total breakroom cost is $440–$961 per month. On a quarterly deep clean schedule, divide the per-event price by three: $60–$140 per month on top of the routine pass.

blocks.text: Chemicals and tools that affect quality and price

Breakroom deep cleans use more chemistry than most janitorial tasks, and the products a vendor chooses affect labor time. A concentrated degreaser that cuts microwave and hood grease quickly saves time compared with scrubbing with a general-purpose cleaner. Food-contact surfaces need a properly diluted sanitizer with the label's contact time respected, and a final potable water rinse where the label requires it. Glass-front beverage coolers, glass backsplashes, and interior partitions are faster and streak-free with a professional squeegee such as the Ettore Master Brass 14-inch, which has a solid brass handle and replaceable rubber blade.

Many breakrooms in tech and creative offices have carpet tile at the edges or in adjacent lounge seating. Coffee and food spills there need extraction, not just spotting. A portable unit like the Rug Doctor Mighty Pro X3, with a 3.9-gallon recovery tank, 28 PSI pump, and vibrating brush, handles café-edge carpet during the same visit. For larger lounge areas or quarterly contracts, the Sandia Sniper's 6-gallon tank, 100 PSI pump, dual vacuum motors, and 2000W heater pull embedded sugars and oils faster, which lowers billed hours.

blocks.title: Food safety, HazCom, and refrigerator contents
blocks.text: Vendors must supply Safety Data Sheets for every chemical under OSHA HazCom 1910.1200 and use EPA-registered sanitizers on food-contact surfaces at label dilution and contact time. Agree in writing on how employee food is handled during refrigerator clean-outs: typically a posted notice 48 hours ahead and a rule that unlabeled items are discarded. Confirm that the vendor's certificate of insurance is current before the first visit.

faqs.q: What is the typical unit price for a commercial breakroom deep clean?
faqs.a: Nationally, expect $0.35–$0.90 per sq ft of breakroom floor area, $25–$85 per major appliance, or $35–$65 per standard labor hour, with specialty degreasing at $55–$95 per hour. Most vendors apply a $90–$135 minimum per visit.

faqs.q: Is refrigerator interior cleaning included in nightly breakroom service?
faqs.a: Usually not. The standard breakroom add-on of $12–$25 per visit covers counters, sinks, microwave interiors and exteriors, refrigerator exteriors, and cabinet pulls. Interior clean-outs, gasket scrubbing, and coil vacuuming are deep-clean tasks priced separately.

faqs.q: Should janitors descale coffee machines and ice makers?
faqs.a: Only if the equipment owner's service agreement allows it. Janitors typically clean exteriors, drip trays, and ice bins with an approved sanitizer. Internal descaling and ice machine evaporator cleaning normally belong to the equipment service provider, and unauthorized work can void warranties.

faqs.q: How do I keep a small kitchenette from being charged a full minimum?
faqs.a: Bundle the deep clean with a nightly visit or another periodic task, such as interior glass or carpet spotting, so the $90–$135 minimum covers more work. Confirm the contract treats the minimum as a floor, not an add-on to unit pricing.

faqs.q: What compliance documents should a breakroom deep cleaning vendor provide?
faqs.a: A current certificate of insurance naming your company and landlord, Safety Data Sheets for all chemicals under OSHA HazCom, EPA registration numbers for sanitizers used on food-contact surfaces, and a written food handling and disposal procedure for refrigerator clean-outs.
